promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Carrying out and monitoring the PEP

questions.q: In the context of setting PEP targets, what does the acronym SMART stand for?
options: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound
Simple, Manageable, Actionable, Reliable, Timely
Strategic, Measured, Agreed, Recorded, Trained
Specific, Meaningful, Attainable, Repeated, Tested
questions.explain: SMART targets are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound, giving clear goals to plan a PEP around.

questions.q: What do the four letters of the FITT principle represent?
options: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type
Fitness, Interval, Training, Threshold
Frequency, Interval, Timing, Technique
Force, Intensity, Tempo, Type
questions.explain: FITT (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type) is used to apply progressive overload when planning and adjusting a PEP.

questions.q: Why is fitness testing carried out before a PEP begins?
options: To establish baseline (pre-test) data to measure progress against
To warm the performer up before every session
To decide which sport the performer should take up
To replace the need for a final evaluation
questions.explain: Pre-PEP fitness tests provide baseline data so improvement can be measured when tests are repeated at the end.

questions.q: Which formula is used to estimate a performer's maximum heart rate?
options: 220 minus age
210 minus half the age
200 plus age
Resting heart rate multiplied by 3
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 minus the performer's age in years.

questions.q: According to Edexcel, what percentage range of maximum heart rate defines the aerobic training zone?
questions.explain: The aerobic training zone is 60-80% of maximum heart rate, developing cardiovascular endurance.

questions.q: Which percentage range of maximum heart rate defines the anaerobic training zone?
questions.explain: The anaerobic training zone lies at 80-90% of maximum heart rate, developing speed and power without oxygen.

questions.q: The Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) scale runs across which range of numbers?
options: 6 to 20
1 to 10
1 to 20
questions.explain: The Borg RPE scale runs from 6 (no exertion) to 20 (maximal exertion).

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of continuous training?
options: Jogging at a steady pace for 30 minutes
Alternating sprints and rest in fixed sets
Completing stations at a circuit
Lifting weights in repetitions and sets
questions.explain: Continuous training involves sustained, steady-state aerobic exercise without rest periods.

questions.q: Why should PEP targets be 'measurable'?
options: So progress can be objectively tracked and compared over time
So the sessions are more enjoyable to complete
So the performer never has to repeat any fitness tests
So the training always stays at the same intensity
questions.explain: Measurable targets allow objective comparison of results so improvement can be judged.

questions.q: What does the principle of progressive overload require during a PEP?
options: Gradually increasing the demands placed on the body over time
Keeping intensity identical in every session
Reducing training frequency each week
Training only the muscles the performer prefers
questions.explain: Progressive overload means gradually increasing training demands so the body continues to adapt and improve.

questions.q: What does the principle of reversibility mean for a performer's PEP?
options: Fitness gains are gradually lost if training stops or reduces
Training must be reversed to the opposite muscle group
Sessions should be performed in reverse order each week
Improvements happen faster the longer training is paused
questions.explain: Reversibility means adaptations are lost when training stops or intensity drops for a prolonged period.

questions.q: How does the principle of specificity influence PEP planning?
options: Training is matched to the demands of the activity or component of fitness
Every session must use the same single method of training
Training targets whichever component is easiest to improve
The programme is identical for every performer regardless of sport
questions.explain: Specificity means the training chosen must be relevant to the performer's sport and targeted fitness components.

questions.q: Why does a performer keep a training diary throughout the PEP?
options: To record and monitor sessions, intensity and progress
To replace the need to warm up
To calculate their maximum heart rate
To decide the aim of the programme after it has ended
questions.explain: A training diary lets the performer monitor adherence, intensity and progress so the PEP can be adjusted.

questions.q: How can an RPE value be used to roughly estimate exercise heart rate?
options: Multiply the RPE value by 10
Add 20 to the RPE value
Divide the RPE value by 2
Subtract the RPE value from 220
questions.explain: Multiplying the Borg RPE value by 10 gives an approximate heart rate in beats per minute.

questions.q: Why is a thorough warm-up included at the start of each PEP session?
options: To prepare the body and reduce the risk of injury
To immediately overload the muscles to failure
To replace the main training component
To lower the heart rate below resting level
questions.explain: A warm-up gradually raises heart rate and muscle temperature, preparing the body and reducing injury risk.

questions.q: Which factor should most influence the choice of training method when planning a PEP?
options: The specific fitness components the performer needs to improve
The colour of the performer's kit
How long the changing rooms are open
The performer's favourite type of music
questions.explain: Training methods are selected to develop the specific components of fitness identified as needing improvement.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of re-testing fitness at the end of a PEP?
options: To compare results with baseline data and judge improvement
To warm the performer down after training
To decide the aim of the programme
To increase the maximum heart rate value
questions.explain: Post-PEP testing is compared against baseline data to evaluate how much fitness has improved.

questions.q: A good PEP evaluation should identify strengths and weaknesses and then...
options: Suggest modifications to improve future programmes
Delete all of the training data collected
Repeat the exact same programme with no changes
Ignore any sessions that were missed
questions.explain: Evaluation reflects on what worked and what did not, recommending modifications for future training.

questions.q: A 15-year-old performer wants to train aerobically. What is their estimated maximum heart rate?
options: 205 bpm
220 bpm
185 bpm
235 bpm
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is 220 minus age, so 220 minus 15 equals 205 bpm.

questions.q: A 20-year-old wants to train at the lower end of the aerobic zone (60% of max HR). What is their target heart rate? (Max HR = 200 bpm)
options: 120 bpm
160 bpm
100 bpm
180 bpm
questions.explain: 60% of a maximum heart rate of 200 bpm is 0.6 multiplied by 200, giving 120 bpm.

questions.q: A marathon runner needs to develop cardiovascular endurance for their PEP. Which training method is most suitable?
options: Continuous training
Plyometric training
Static weight training for maximum strength
Short maximal sprint intervals only
questions.explain: Continuous, steady-state aerobic training best develops the cardiovascular endurance a marathon runner needs.

questions.q: After a six-week PEP, a performer's Cooper 12-minute run distance increases from 2200 m to 2600 m. What does this most clearly show?
options: Improved aerobic (cardiovascular) endurance
Improved flexibility
Improved reaction time
Reduced muscular strength
questions.explain: The Cooper run measures aerobic endurance, so a greater distance shows cardiovascular endurance has improved.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE PE & Sport Science (1PE0) specification; Personal Exercise Programme
